Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavits filed by learned counsel for the applicants are taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2/informant and learned AGA for the State.

3. The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.1706 of 2018 has been filed on behalf of the applicants,
namely, Faraj Zuberi, Suhail Akthar & Shamshad Ahmad for quashing of the entire proceedings,
including charge-sheet dated 16.10.2017 and cognizance/summoning order dated 06.11.2017, of criminal case No. 63624 of 2017, arising out of case crime no. 420 of 2017 (State Vs. Faraj Zuberi &
others), under Sections 147, 323, 504, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B, 447 IPC, P.S. Chakeri, District Kanpur Nagar, pending in the court of CJM, Kanpur Nagar, on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

4. The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No.11226 of 2018 has been filed on behalf of applicant Saud Akhtar in the aforesaid case with same prayer.
5.

It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the matter relates to property dispute, which is essentially civil in nature and first information report of this case was got lodged by moving an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
Now both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter.
The informant of the case does not want to pursue the impugned proceedings.

It was submitted that the compromise filed by the parties before the trial court concerned, has already been verified and the report of compromise and verification report is available on record in supplementary affidavit.

In view of these facts and circumstances, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the impugned proceedings pending and thus, the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 /informant has concurred with the arguments of learned counsel for the applicants and submitted that both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and the informant does not want to proceed with the case pending before the trial court and the impugned proceedings may be quashed, as no useful purpose would be served by exhausting remedy of trial.
5.
Learned A.G.A. has no objection if parties compromise the matter.
6. I have considered the submissions and perused the record.
7. It is well settled that in appropriate cases, criminal proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.
In the instant case, the dispute between the parties relates to property, which is essentially civil and private in nature.
If parties compromise the matter, it would not have adverse impact on society.
There is nothing to indicate that parties have any criminal antecedents.
The informant does not want to proceed with the case against the applicants.
The compromise filed by the parties before the trial court, has already been verified by the court concerned.

Considering the Faraz Zuberi And 2 Ors. vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145827448/
2 law laid down in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296 and the facts of the matter, it would be in the interest of justice that the impugned proceedings be quashed, as the continuance of the same would be nothing but wastage of time of Court.

8. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned charge-sheet/cognizance-summoning order and entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case against applicants, namely, Faraj Zuberi, Suhail Akthar,
Shamshad Ahmad & Saud Akhtar
are hereby quashed.
9. Both the applications u/s 482 Cr.P.C. are allowed.
